heading: PROTECTION OF CHILDREN AND WOMEN
translated_text:
PROTECTION OF CHILDREN AND WOMEN

MAYOR OF SINGKAWANG

PROVINCE OF WEST KALIMANTAN

heading: REGIONAL REGULATION OF SINGKAWANG CITY
CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the City of Singkawang.
2. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Singkawang City.
4. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including those still in the womb.
5. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
6. Victim is a child and woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
7. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, the community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
8. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
9. Special protection is a form of protection received by children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development.
10. Violence against women and children, hereinafter referred to as violence, is any act based on gender differences that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and hindering the ability of women and children to enjoy all their rights and freedoms.
11. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
12. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
13. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises parental authority as a parent over a child.
14. Every person is an individual or corporation, whether a legal entity or not a legal entity.
15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and/or knowing that violence against the victim will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
16. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, to strengthen victims of violence to resolve the problems they face.
17. Regional Apparatus Organization, hereinafter abbreviated as OPD, is a regional apparatus organization within the Singkawang City Government.
18. Prevention is an activity carried out so that acts of violence against children and women do not occur.
19. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence to their families, substitute families or communities that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
20. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions so that they can carry out their roles again properly both in the family and in society.
21. Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with families, communities, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection.
22. Institution is an agency/office/body/office within the scope of the Regional Government and/or non-governmental organizations that provide assistance.
23. Agency is a regional apparatus work unit whose duties and responsibilities are to coordinate the handling of affairs in the field of organizing child and women protection.
24. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
25. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated, one-stop, and networked technical service established by the government, Regional Government, community, non-governmental organizations, donor institutions, and other institutions in efforts to empower women and protect women and children comprehensively from various types of discrimination and violence, including human trafficking.
26. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations, and/or community organizations.
27. Regional Action Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RAD, is a foundation and guideline for relevant agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in carrying out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of children and women victims of violence.
28. Task Force is a coordinating body established by the Regional Government that coordinates policies, programs, and activities for the protection of children and women in the region.
29. Child-Friendly City, hereinafter abbreviated as KLA, is a city that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of the commitment and resources of the Regional Government, community, and business world that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs, and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.

heading: CHAPTER II
Article 3
heading_path: RIGHTS OF CHILDREN, WOMEN, AND VICTIMS

heading: Article 4
heading_path: RIGHTS OF CHILDREN, WOMEN, AND VICTIMS
translated_text:
Article 4

Every victim has the right to report and receive assistance as well as receive guarantees of their rights related to their status as a wife, mother, child, family member as well as a community member.

heading: Article 5
heading_path: RIGHTS OF CHILDREN, WOMEN, AND VICTIMS
translated_text:
Article 5

The rights as referred to in Article 2 paragraph (3) letter c, are also given to the families of witnesses and/or victims up to the second degree, if the families of witnesses and/or victims receive threats either physical or psychological from other people relating to the testimony of witnesses and/or victims.

heading: CHAPTER III
CHAPTER IV
translated_text:
CHAPTER IV

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Article 7

The obligations and responsibilities of organizers of child and women protection are the joint responsibility of the Regional Government, community, family, and parents or guardians.

heading: Article 8
Article 9
translated_text:
Article 9

1. The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 7 are organized in the form of community participation in organizing child and women protection.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), can be carried out in the form of:
a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. submitting reports to the authorities if acts of violence against women and children occur;
c. providing assistance to victims; and
d. playing an active role in efforts to increase the fulfillment of children's rights and women's empowerment.
3. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) is carried out by individuals, social community institutions, community organizations, professional organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, private sector, mass media, and the business world.
4. The role of community organizations, professional organizations, and educational institutions is carried out by taking necessary steps in accordance with the respective duties, functions, authorities, and competencies to assist in organizing child and women protection.
5. The role of mass media is carried out through the dissemination of information and educational materials related to organizing child and women protection by taking into account the best interests of children and/or victims.
6. The role of the business world is carried out through:
a. company policies with child and women perspectives;
b. products intended must be safe for children; and
c. contributing to the fulfillment of children's rights and women's empowerment through corporate social responsibility.
7. Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (2), are implemented responsibly in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

heading: Article 10
translated_text:
Article 10

The obligations and responsibilities of the family as referred to in Article 7, legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women and children as family members.

heading: Article 11
CHAPTER V
translated_text:
CHAPTER V

STATUS OF CHILDREN

Part One

Identity of Children

heading: Article 12
translated_text:
Article 12

1. The identity of every child must be given from birth.
2. The identity as referred to in paragraph (1) is set forth in a birth certificate.
3. The making of a birth certificate is based on a certificate from the person who witnessed and/or assisted the birth process.
4. In the case of a child whose birth process is unknown, and whose parents are unknown whereabouts, the making of a birth certificate for that child is based on the statement of the person who found and completed by a police investigation report.

heading: Article 13
translated_text:
Article 13

1. The organizer of making birth certificates is carried out by the Regional Apparatus Organization that administers population administration affairs.
2. Provisions regarding procedures and requirements for making birth certificates as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

heading: Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Children Born from Mixed Marriages

heading: Article 14
translated_text:
Article 14

1. If a mixed marriage occurs between a citizen of the Republic of Indonesia and a foreign citizen, the child born from that marriage is entitled to obtain the citizenship of his father or mother in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.
2. In the event of divorce from the marriage as referred to in paragraph (1), the child has the right to choose or based on a court decision, to be in the custody of one of both parents.
3. In the event of divorce as referred to in paragraph (2), while the child is not yet able to determine a choice, and his mother is a citizen of the Republic of Indonesia, for the best interests of the child or at the request of his mother, the Regional Government is obliged to arrange the citizenship status of the Republic of Indonesia for the child concerned.

heading: CHAPTER VI
translated_text:
CHAPTER VI

CUSTODY

Article 15

1. In the event that parents as referred to in Article 11 paragraph (1) neglect their obligations, supervisory action may be taken against them or parental custody may be revoked.
2. Supervisory action against parents or revocation of custody as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through a court order.

JDIH Kota Singkawang

heading: Article 16
translated_text:
Article 16

1. One of the parents, biological siblings or family up to the third degree, may submit an application to the court to obtain a court order regarding revocation of parental custody or to take supervisory action if there are strong reasons for it as referred to in Article 15 paragraph (1).
2. If one of the parents, biological siblings, or family up to the third degree, cannot carry out their function, then the revocation of parental custody as referred to in paragraph (1) may also be submitted by an authorized official or other institution that has the authority to do so.
3. The court order as referred to in paragraph (1) may appoint an individual or government/community institution to become a guardian for the child concerned.
4. Individuals who carry out child care as referred to in paragraph (3) must be of the same religion as the religion adhered to by the child to be cared for.

heading: CHAPTER VII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VII

GUARDIANSHIP

Article 17

1. In the event that a child is not capable of performing legal acts, while the parents or family are not known residence or whereabouts, then a person or legal entity that meets the requirements may be appointed as guardian of the child concerned.
2. To become a guardian of a child as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through a court order.
3. The appointed guardian's religion must be the same as the religion adhered to by the child.
4. The guardian appointed as referred to in paragraph (2) is responsible for the child and must manage the property of the child concerned for the best interests of the child.
5. Provisions regarding the requirements and procedures for appointing a guardian are implemented in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

JDIH Kota Singkawang

heading: CHAPTER VIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VIII

ADOPTION OF CHILDREN

Article 18

1. Adoption of children may only be carried out for the best interests of the child, and is carried out based on customs and in accordance with Laws and Regulations.
2. Adoption of children does not sever blood relations between the adopted child and his biological parents.
3. Adoption of children must be recorded in the birth certificate without eliminating the child's initial identity.
4. Prospective adoptive parents must be of the same religion as the religion adhered to by the prospective adopted child.
5. Adoption of children by foreign citizens may only be carried out as a last resort in accordance with Laws and Regulations.
6. In the event that the child's origin is unknown, then the child's religion is adjusted to the religion of the majority of the local population.

heading: Article 19
translated_text:
Article 19

1. Adoptive parents are obliged to inform their adopted child about his origin and biological parents.
2. Notification of origin and biological parents is carried out with due regard to the child's mental readiness.

heading: CHAPTER IX
translated_text:
CHAPTER IX

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION

Part One

General

heading: Article 20
Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Planning and Development of Information Systems for Children and Women

heading: Article 21
translated_text:
Article 21

1. Planning for the protection of children and women is implemented by providing data and information related to the protection of children and women in the region.
2. Data and information as referred to in paragraph (1) concerns data on gender mainstreaming (PUG), data on mainstreaming children's rights (PUHA), and evaluation of programs and data services.
3. Data and information as referred to in paragraph (2) is provided by the Regional Apparatus Organization that administers child and women protection affairs.
4. Information data as referred to in paragraph (3) is needed for policy planning and program intervention coordinated by the Agency.

heading: Part Three
translated_text:
Part Three

Prevention and Protection

heading: Article 22
Article 23
translated_text:
Article 23

1. Every Person and/or Institution is obliged to protect children and women from violence, exploitation, discrimination, maltreatment and neglect.
2. Protection by Institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) by not implementing policies and actions that violate the rights of children and women.

heading: Part Four
translated_text:
Part Four

Child Protection

heading: Paragraph 1
translated_text:
Paragraph 1

Religion

heading: Article 24
translated_text:
Article 24

1. Every child receives protection to worship according to their religion.
2. Before a child can determine their choice, the religion embraced by the child follows the religion of their parents.

heading: Article 25
translated_text:
Article 25

1. Regional Government, community, family, parents, guardians, and community social institutions guarantee the protection of children in embracing their religion.
2. Protection of children in embracing their religion as referred to in paragraph (1), includes guidance, mentoring, and practice of religious teachings for children.

heading: Paragraph 2
translated_text:
Paragraph 2

Health

heading: Article 26
translated_text:
Article 26

1. Regional Government is obliged to provide facilities and organize comprehensive health efforts for children, so that every child obtains optimal health status from the womb.
2. Provision of facilities and organization of comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1), is supported by community participation.
3. Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) include promotive, preventive, curative, and rehabilitative efforts, both for basic health services and referrals.
4. Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (3) are organized free of charge for families who are unable to afford it.
(5) Implementation of provisions as referred to in paragraph (1) through paragraph (4) is carried out in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

heading: Article 27
translated_text:
Article 27

1. Parents and family are obliged to be responsible for maintaining the health of children and caring for children from the womb.
2. In the event that parents and family are unable to carry out their responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1), then the Regional Government is obliged to fulfill it.
3. Obligations as referred to in paragraph (2), are implemented in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

heading: Article 28
translated_text:
Article 28

Every person is prohibited from performing abortion on a child still in the womb, except for reasons and procedures justified in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

heading: Article 29
translated_text:
Article 29

Regional Government, community, family, and parents or guardians are obliged to protect children from actions that disturb the health and development of children.

JDIH Kota Singkawang

heading: Paragraph 3
translated_text:
Paragraph 3

Education

heading: Article 30
translated_text:
Article 30

1. Regional Government is obliged to organize basic education of at least 9 (nine) years for all children.
2. Parents are obliged to fulfill the child's right to obtain basic education of at least 9 (nine) years.

heading: Article 31
translated_text:
Article 31

Regional Government, family, and parents or guardians are obliged to provide the widest possible opportunity for children to obtain education.

heading: Article 32
Article 33
translated_text:
Article 33

1. Children with disabilities are given opportunities and accessibility to obtain inclusive education and/or special education.
2. Children who have excellence are given opportunities and accessibility to obtain special education.
3. Children who receive special protection are given opportunities to obtain their right to education.

heading: Article 34
translated_text:
Article 34

1. Regional Government is responsible for providing education costs and/or free or special services for children from underprivileged families, neglected children, and children residing in remote areas.
2. Regional Government responsibility as referred to in paragraph (1) also includes encouraging the community to play an active role.

heading: Article 35
translated_text:
Article 35

1. Children in the education unit environment must receive protection from physical violence, psychological violence, sexual crimes, and other crimes committed by educators, educational institutions, fellow students and/or other parties.
2. Protection as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by educators, education personnel, government officials and/or the community.

heading: Article 36
translated_text:
Article 36

(1) Regional Government is obliged to develop a child-friendly school model.
(2) Child-friendly schools as referred to in paragraph (1) constitute a joint effort of school members to:
a. create a safe and comfortable environment for children at school;
b. develop child participation in accordance with their age and maturity; and
c. provide opportunities for children from poor families and/or persons with disabilities to receive equal and fair treatment to obtain services and guidance at school.

heading: Paragraph 4
translated_text:
Paragraph 4

Social

heading: Article 37
translated_text:
Article 37

1. Regional Government is obliged to organize maintenance and care of neglected children, both in institutions and outside institutions.
2. Organization of maintenance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by institutions or the community.
3. To organize maintenance and care of neglected children by institutions and the community, as referred to in paragraph (2), may establish cooperation with various related parties.
4. In the case of organizing maintenance and care as referred to in paragraph (3), supervision is carried out by the Regional Apparatus organizing social affairs in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

heading: Article 38
Article 39
translated_text:
Article 39

In the event a child is neglected because their parents neglect their obligations, then the institution or community as referred to in Article 37, family or authorized official may submit an application to the court to determine the child as a neglected child.

heading: Article 40
translated_text:
Article 40

1. Court determination as referred to in Article 39 simultaneously determines the place of shelter, maintenance and care of the neglected child concerned.
2. Institutions or communities granted authority are obliged to provide a place as referred to in paragraph (1).
3. Regional Government is obliged to conduct guidance and support the smooth care of children carried out by institutions or communities.

heading: Part Five
translated_text:
Part Five

Special Protection

heading: Article 41
Article 42
Article 43
Article 44
translated_text:
Article 44

Special protection for children who become refugees as in Article 43 letter a is implemented in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

heading: Article 45
translated_text:
Article 45

Special protection for child victims of unrest, disaster victims, and children in armed conflict situations as referred to in Article 43 letters b through letter d is implemented through:
a. fulfillment of basic needs consisting of food, clothing, housing, education, health, learning, and recreation, security guarantees, and equal treatment; and
b. fulfillment of special needs for children with disabilities and children experiencing psychosocial disorders.

heading: Article 46
Article 47
translated_text:
Article 47

Special protection for children from minority and isolated groups as referred to in Article 41 letter c is carried out through provision of infrastructure and facilities to be able to enjoy their own culture, acknowledge and practice their own religion, and use their own language.

heading: Article 48
translated_text:
Article 48

Special protection for children who are exploited economically and/or sexually as referred to in Article 41 letter d is carried out through:
a. dissemination and/or socialization of provisions of Laws and Regulations related to protection of children who are exploited economically and/or sexually;
b. monitoring, reporting, and imposition of sanctions; and
c. involvement of various institutions or government agencies, companies, labor unions, social community institutions, and the community in eliminating exploitation of children economically and/or sexually.

heading: Article 49
translated_text:
Article 49

Special protection for children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substance abuse as referred to in Article 41 letter e and involved in their production and distribution is carried out through efforts of supervision, prevention, treatment, and rehabilitation by Regional Government and community.

heading: Article 50
translated_text:
Article 50

1. Special protection for children who are victims of pornography as referred to in Article 41 letter f is implemented through efforts of guidance, assistance, and social, physical health, and mental recovery.
2. Guidance, assistance and social, physical health, and mental recovery are implemented in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.
3. Every person is obliged to protect children from the influence of pornography and prevent children's access to information containing elements of pornography.

heading: Article 51
translated_text:
Article 51

Special protection for children with human immunodeficiency virus/acquired immune deficiency syndrome as referred to in Article 41 letter g is carried out through efforts of supervision, prevention, treatment, care, and rehabilitation.

heading: Article 52
translated_text:
Article 52

Special protection for child victims of abduction, sale, and child trafficking as referred to in Article 41 letter h is carried out through efforts of supervision, protection, prevention, care, and rehabilitation by Regional Government and community.

heading: Article 53
translated_text:
Article 53

Special protection for child victims of physical and/or psychological violence as referred to in Article 41 letter i is carried out through efforts of:
a. dissemination and socialization of provisions of Laws and Regulations that protect child victims of acts of violence; and
b. monitoring, reporting, and imposition of sanctions.

heading: Article 54
Article 55
Article 56
translated_text:
Article 56

Special protection for children with special needs as referred to in Article 41 letter I shall be carried out through efforts to:
a. treat children humanely in accordance with the dignity and rights of the child; JDIH Kota Singkawang
b. fulfill the special needs of the child; and
c. obtain equal treatment with other children to achieve full social integration and individual development as much as possible.

heading: Article 57
translated_text:
Article 57

Special protection for child victims of abuse and neglect as referred to in Article 41 letter m shall be carried out through supervision, prevention, care, counseling, rehabilitation and assistance by the Regional Government and the community.

heading: Article 58
translated_text:
Article 58

Special protection for children with deviant social behavior as referred to in Article 41 letter n shall be carried out through guidance on religious values and social values, counseling, rehabilitation and assistance by the Regional Government and the community.

heading: Article 59
translated_text:
Article 59

Special protection for children who become victims of stigmatization from labeling related to their parents' condition as referred to in Article 41 letter o shall be carried out through counseling, rehabilitation and assistance by the Regional Government and the community.

heading: Article 60
translated_text:
Article 60

Further provisions regarding special protection for children as referred to in Article 41 letter a through letter o shall be regulated by Mayor Regulation.

heading: Article 61
translated_text:
Article 61

Every child who becomes a victim as referred to in Article 41 letter d, letter f, letter h, letter i, and letter j has the right to file a claim in court in the form of the right to restitution which is the responsibility of the perpetrator of the crime in accordance with applicable provisions.

heading: Part Six
translated_text:
Part Six

Protection of Women

heading: Article 62
Part Seven
translated_text:
Part Seven

Protection in the Workplace

heading: Article 63
translated_text:
Article 63

1. Every company is prohibited from recruiting child labor under age or exploiting children.
2. Companies must position female workers as work partners to grow the company.

heading: Article 64
Article 65
translated_text:
Article 65

1. Female workers who work beyond working hours, the company is obligated to provide overtime pay in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.
2. Companies are obligated to protect occupational health and safety, and provide maternity leave rights to female workers.
3. Companies are prohibited from making policies that cause discrimination against female workers.
4. Companies that violate the provisions as referred to in paragraph (1), paragraph (2), and paragraph (3), may be subject to administrative sanctions in the form of:
a. verbal warning;
b. written warning; and
c. other administrative sanctions in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

heading: Part Eight
translated_text:
Part Eight

Handling

heading: Article 66
Article 67
translated_text:
Article 67

1. Identification and receipt of complaints/reports as referred to in Article 66 paragraph (2) letter a includes:
a. ensuring readiness for complaints regarding child and women protection issues;
b. following up on information or complaints/reports received regarding child and women protection issues; and
c. identifying the type of problem, needs and handling plan.
2. The Regional Apparatus Organization responsible for women's empowerment and child protection affairs is obligated to identify problems and receive complaints/reports.

heading: Article 68
translated_text:
Article 68

1. Rescue actions as referred to in Article 66 paragraph (2) letter b are carried out if based on identification results it is known that the safety of the child or woman victim of violence is threatened.
2. Actions as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by removing the child from the situation and environment that poses a threat.
3. The Regional Apparatus Organization responsible for women's empowerment and child protection affairs is obligated to carry out rescue actions and coordinate with police officers or civil service police units.

heading: Article 69
translated_text:
Article 69

1. Placement of children or women victims of violence in temporary shelters as referred to in Article 66 paragraph (2) letter c is carried out if based on identification results:
a. there is a threat to safety;
b. the child has no family/caregiver or guardian; and/or
c. the child cannot be reunited with family/caregiver/guardian and/or the community.
2. Placement as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out for a certain period of time while the child or victim receives recovery services and/or until the family/caregiver/guardian is assessed to have readiness to care for and protect the child.
3. Services provided to children and/or women while in temporary shelters include services for fulfilling basic needs and psychosocial support.
4. The Regional Apparatus Organization responsible for social affairs is obligated to provide temporary shelters.
5. The Regional Apparatus Organization responsible for social affairs may cooperate with civil service police or the police in efforts to maintain the security of children or women whose safety is threatened while in temporary shelters.

heading: Article 70
Article 71
Article 72
translated_text:
Article 72

1. Legal assistance support services as referred to in Article 66 paragraph (2) letter d number 3 include:
a. ensuring children are accompanied by legal counsel; and
b. facilitating assistance to children and women victims of violence, both in the examination process in court proceedings and outside court proceedings.
2. The Regional Apparatus Organization responsible for women's empowerment and child protection affairs is obligated to provide or coordinate legal assistance services with relevant agencies.

heading: Article 73
Article 74
translated_text:
Article 74

1. Handling as referred to in Article 67 through Article 73 is implemented synergistically.
2. Implementation of handling as referred to in paragraph (1) is coordinated by the Regional Apparatus Organization responsible for women's empowerment and child protection affairs.
3. Further provisions regarding technical implementation of handling of children and women are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

JDIH Kota Singkawang

heading: Part Nine
translated_text:
Part Nine

Law Enforcement and Legal Aid Services

heading: Article 75
translated_text:
Article 75

1. Law enforcement services constitute actions by law enforcement officers in implementing Laws and Regulations to handle cases of violence against children and women, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.
2. Law enforcement services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of children and women victims of violence.
3. Law enforcement services are aimed at providing protection to children and women victims of violence or children in conflict with the law with a gender-responsive approach so that victims and perpetrators obtain justice and legal certainty.
4. For the implementation of law enforcement as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Government cooperates with relevant agencies and institutions to allocate resources to encourage the achievement of effectiveness and efficiency of law enforcement services for children and women victims of violence and children in conflict with the law in accordance with applicable provisions.

heading: Article 76
translated_text:
Article 76

Types of legal aid services for children and women victims of violence and children in conflict with the law include:
a. litigation legal aid; and
b. non-litigation legal aid.

heading: Part Ten
translated_text:
Part Ten

Facilitation of Juvenile Criminal Justice

heading: Article 77
Part Eleven
translated_text:
Part Eleven

Empowerment

heading: Article 78
translated_text:
Article 78

1. Empowerment is implemented in the form of:
a. facilitating the development of interests and talents for children and women;
b. developing economic enterprises for adult women;
c. developing creative spaces for children and women; and
d. assistance for children and women victims of violence.
2. Implementation of empowerment as referred to in paragraph (1) may cooperate with educational institutions, private institutions and/or non-governmental organizations.

heading: CHAPTER X
Article 80
translated_text:
Article 80

1. P2TP2A is an integrated, one-stop and networked technical service unit for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection established by the government, Regional Government, community, non-governmental organizations, donor institutions or other institutions.
2. P2TP2A is positioned under the coordination of the Regional Apparatus Organization that handles women's empowerment and child protection.
3. P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) does not have the authority to formulate policies on women's empowerment and child protection.
4. P2TP2A is one form of integrated service unit that functions as:
a. an information center for children and women;
b. a service center for children and women victims of violence; and
c. an empowerment center for children and women.

heading: Article 81
translated_text:
Article 81

1. P2TP2A is established based on a Mayor's Decree.
2. P2TP2A membership comes from structural and non-structural elements originating from professionals, academics, community leaders and other elements as needed.
3. Further provisions regarding the technical aspects of P2TP2A shall be regulated by Mayor Regulation.

heading: Article 82
translated_text:
Article 82

1. In order to increase the effectiveness of supervision of the implementation of children's rights fulfillment, the Regional Government may establish a Regional Child Protection Commission or other similar institutions to support supervision of the implementation of child protection in the region.
2. The membership of the Regional Child Protection Commission consists of 1 (one) chairperson, 1 (one) vice chairperson, and 7 (seven) members.
3. The membership of the Regional Child Protection Commission comes from elements of the Regional Government, religious leaders, community leaders, community organizations, business community, and community groups concerned with child protection.

heading: Article 83
Article 84
translated_text:
Article 84

In the event of changes to Laws and Regulations concerning the Regional Child Protection Commission, the regulation regarding the Regional Child Protection Commission shall be guided by laws and regulations which shall be further regulated by Mayor Regulation.

CHAPTER XI

heading: CHILD-FRIENDLY CITY
translated_text:
CHILD-FRIENDLY CITY

Article 85

To ensure the fulfillment of children's rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination, real and integrated efforts are needed between the Regional Government, community and business community through the development of CFC.

heading: Article 86
Article 87
Article 88
Article 89
translated_text:
Article 89

1. To make the development of CFC effective, a CFC Task Force shall be established as determined by Mayor's Decree.
2. Membership of the CFC Task Force may come from the Regional Government, child representatives, business community, religious leaders, community leaders and other parties as needed.

JDIH Kota Singkawang

heading: Article 90
CHAPTER XII
translated_text:
CHAPTER XII

CHILD PARTICIPATION

Article 91

1. Every child has the right to participate in expressing opinions, ideas, thoughts and others as well as being involved in decision-making processes concerning their lives either directly or indirectly, regarding everything related to themselves and implemented based on awareness, understanding according to age and level of maturity of thinking, as well as mutual willingness so that Children can enjoy the results or obtain benefits from such decisions.
2. Child participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out through the establishment of a Children's Forum.
3. The Children's Forum as referred to in paragraph (2), is an organization whose members are children who become administrators of children's organizations, studios or children's activity groups and the like which are generally based on the development of talents, interests, abilities and utilization of leisure time.
4. The Children's Forum is directly fostered by the Regional Government and is intended to increase the capacity of children who have been active in various organizations in certain fields.
5. In fostering the Children's Forum, the Regional Government may cooperate with professional organizations, community institutions, child-responsive business community.
6. The establishment of the Children's Forum as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be determined by Mayor's Decree.

heading: Article 92
translated_text:
Article 92

1. In every formulation of policies related to Children, the Regional Government must pay attention to and accommodate the opinions of children submitted through the Children's Forum.
2. The Regional Government may include representatives of the Children's Forum in the Regional Development Planning Deliberation.

heading: CHAPTER XIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER XIII

FUNDING AND REPORTING

Article 93

( 1) Funding for the implementation of policies, programs and activities for Child and Women Protection in the region may be sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget;
b. Provincial Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget;
c. National Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
d. other legal and non-binding sources.
2. Funding as referred to in paragraph ( 1) letter a, is based on the needs and financial capacity of the region.

heading: CHAPTER XIV
translated_text:
CHAPTER XIV

GUIDANCE, SUPERVISION AND REPORTING

Article 94

1. The Mayor has the authority to conduct guidance in the implementation of child and women protection.
2. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be implemented in the form of:
a. guidelines and fulfillment standards;
b. technical guidance and training;
c. provision of facilities;
d. monitoring; and
e. evaluation.
3. In the context of guidance as referred to in paragraph (2), the Regional Government may cooperate with the Central Government, other Regional Governments, Non-Governmental Organizations, business community and universities.
4. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be implemented through OPD according to their duties and functions.

heading: Article 95
translated_text:
Article 95

1. The Mayor is obliged to supervise the implementation of child and women protection in the region.
2. The community may supervise the implementation of child and women protection organized by the Regional Government with a mechanism for conveying aspirations to the Mayor or the Regional House of Representatives.

heading: Article 96
translated_text:
Article 96

1. OPD that organize child and women protection are obliged to report the implementation related to their duties and responsibilities in organizing child and women protection to the Mayor.
2. Reporting as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be submitted in writing, covering:
a. administration;
b. finance;
c. services; and
d. performance.
3. Submission of written reports as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be carried out at least once every 3 (three) months.

heading: CHAPTER XV
translated_text:
CHAPTER XV

AWARDS

Article 97

1. The Regional Government may grant awards to any person and/or institution that is fully committed to paying attention to the implementation of child and women protection.
2. Awards as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be in the form of certificates and/or other forms.
3. Further provisions regarding the procedures for granting awards as referred to in paragraph (1), and paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Mayor's Regulation.

heading: CHAPTER XVI
CHAPTER XVII
CHAPTER XVIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER XVIII

PROVISIONS ON SANCTIONS

Article 100

1. Institutions or bodies designated by the Mayor to carry out service tasks that violate service principles may be subject to administrative sanctions.
2. Perpetrators of acts of violence are subject to criminal sanctions in accordance with applicable Laws.
3. Every person who intentionally does not provide protection to women and children resulting in the occurrence of violence, allows violence to occur, does not report and does not provide protection to victims, is subject to sanctions as stipulated in applicable Laws and Regulations.

heading: CHAPTER XIX
translated_text:
CHAPTER XIX

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 101

Implementing regulations of this Regional Regulation shall be stipulated no later than 6 (six) months from the promulgation of this Regional Regulation.

translated_text:

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF SINGKAWANG CITY

NUMBER 4 YEAR 2017 CONCERNING PROTECTION OF CHILDREN AND WOMEN

heading: I. GENERAL
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF SINGKAWANG CITY
translated_text:
I. GENERAL

The implementation of protection for children and women is carried out based on the principles of humanity, integration and justice. Therefore, every person must receive their right to protection for a sense of security and freedom from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity which is contrary to what is aspired to in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, namely the realization of a just and civilized humanity.

In Article 2 of Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, the implementation of Child Protection is based on Pancasila and grounded in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia as well as the basic principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child including:
a. non-discrimination;
b. the best interests of the child;
c. the right to life, survival, and development; and d. respect for the views of the child.

In Article 3 of Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, the elimination of domestic violence is implemented based on the principles of:
a. respect for human rights;
b. justice and gender equality,
c. non-discrimination; and
d. protection of victims.

In Article 3 of Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Child Protection aims to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from JDIH Kota Singkawang violence and discrimination, for the realization of quality Indonesian children who are virtuous and prosperous.

In Article 4 of Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, the elimination of domestic violence aims to: a. prevent all forms of violence in the household;
b. protect victims of domestic violence;
c. prosecute perpetrators of domestic violence; and
d. maintain the integrity of a harmonious and prosperous household.
To realize law enforcement and the fulfillment of the basic rights of children and women, the Government of Singkawang City is obliged to provide protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as the fulfillment of civil rights and freedoms which are set forth in a policy at the regional level.

The establishment of a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Children and Women is an elaboration of higher legislation that regulates the rights of children and women. In the Regional Regulation on the Protection of Children and Women, the norms formulated are efforts to address the problems faced in the implementation of child and women protection in Singkawang City.
The implementation of child and women protection is carried out to realize the fulfillment of the rights of children and women in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and to receive protection from violence, discrimination, exploitation, and neglect for the realization of human resource development in Singkawang City that is faithful, intelligent, quality, virtuous and prosperous.
